A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Time-VLM study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete Appendices A–D are readable and support comparison. Appendix content can be matched across renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original Time-VLM forecasting experiments, component ablations, computational measurements, sensitivity analyses, and prediction examples in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results and adds memory-branch ablations, representation-alignment analysis, and VLM-backbone comparisons in Section 4.5.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 substantially changes the specified RAL procedure. v1 uses learnable memory queries attending to patches and gated local/global fusion. v2 specifies a circular historical-memory buffer, top-k similarity retrieval, a two-layer MLP with residual integration, pooled self-attention, and additive local/global fusion. These change the proposed computation, beyond additional explanation.

E1.justification: v2 adds MSCOCO image-caption data for the representation-alignment analysis in Section 4.5 and Figure 4. Forecasting coverage remains the same: ETT, Weather, ECL, Traffic, and M4, with the existing few-shot, zero-shot, short-term, and long-term tasks.

E2.justification: New Table 8 evaluates CLIP and BLIP-2 alternatives to ViLT and a Custom comparator combining ViT-B/16 with BERT-Base. v1 mentions alternative VLM support but reports no corresponding comparison. Comparator membership in the main forecasting tables and Appendix B is unchanged.

E3.justification: New analyses introduce sampling of 400 MSCOCO pairs and 200 samples from each stated time-series dataset, embedding comparisons using VLM, ViT, and BERT, and different backbone configurations. Table 6 changes from MSE/MAE to MSE-only reporting. Existing benchmark splits, forecasting horizons, training budgets, and Appendix A settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands tests of the architecture's rationale: Table 6 separately removes local and global memory; Figure 4 examines alignment with natural image/text representations; and Table 8 tests backbone choice and pretrained cross-modal alignment against separate encoders. Existing whole-component ablations, sensitivity studies, and appendix prediction examples are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Averages over forecasting horizons and gate-weight distributions are retained; the new analyses do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantive architecture results: Weather MSE averages of 0.273 without local memory and 0.243 without global memory, versus 0.233 for the full model; and ETTh2 backbone MSEs of 0.336, 0.339, 0.342, and 0.348 for ViLT, CLIP, BLIP-2, and Custom. It also adds embedding-analysis findings and removes Table 6's MAE results. Tables 1–5, Table 7, and Appendix B retain their values; the additions do not establish a between-version performance gain.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 replaces the learnable-query attention and gated-memory equations with definitions for similarity retrieval, local-memory transformation, pooled self-attention, and additive fusion. This is a localized revision of mathematical definitions. Other substantive formulas remain unchanged, and neither version provides theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the central contribution: unifying temporal, visual, and textual representations through pretrained VLMs and three learners, with efficient forecasting and particular strengths in few-shot and zero-shot settings. Rewriting and new supporting analyses do not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantial interpretations about COCO-pair embeddings mediating cross-modal alignment and pretrained alignment providing an advantage over separate encoders. It discusses why larger VLMs need not improve accuracy and extends hyperparameter interpretations. The conclusion newly acknowledges full-shot shortcomings on ECL/Traffic and deployment constraints; these qualifications extend the unchanged appendix limitations.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability statement and repository address in the abstract and identifies ViT-B/16 and BERT-Base for the new Custom comparison. Existing hardware, optimization, preprocessing, and default hyperparameter disclosures in Appendix A remain unchanged. Repository availability is stated in the PDF, not independently verified.

R1.justification: The bibliography retains the same cited works. Section 2 preserves its text-augmented, vision-augmented, and VLM groupings and the same research-gap positioning, despite extensive paraphrasing.

P1.justification: Existing prose is extensively rewritten across the introduction, related work, methodology, experimental discussion, and conclusion. Forecasting subsections gain explicit Setting and Results paragraphs, TAL explanations are condensed, and the conclusion gains a labeled limitations discussion. Acknowledgements and publication information are added; appendix organization is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the alignment visualization in Figure 4 and backbone-comparison Table 8, restructures Table 6 around MSE and memory branches, and redraws Figure 3 and the sensitivity panels with revised labels, legends, and styling. The main-text displays are substantially revised. Appendix figures and tables are retained with renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful component and backbone controls, code-access information, and explicit performance and deployment limitations. However, its revised historical-retrieval procedure in Section 3.1 is not reconciled with Appendix A.2's retained learnable-query configuration or the unchanged benchmark results. New claims about embedding overlap and mediation also go beyond what Figure 4 clearly establishes. These benefits and new methodological and interpretive ambiguities prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
